title: Finance 1:1 prep - run-rate & procurement (Jordan)
content:
Meeting: 1:1 w/ CPO (Thu 10am) - focus: run-rate review, upcoming procurement approvals, contract renewals, quick FYI on cloud spend trends.

Purpose: quick sync to align on top-level run-rate assumptions and get sign-off path for two procurement items (GPU reserved capacity and analytics data retention add-on). Need CPO buy-in for timing and any product tradeoffs.

High-level run-rate (current month):
- Revenue-recurring run-rate: $1.85M/mo (hosted API + Dedicated contracts).
- Gross burn: ~$1.72M/mo (incl hiring ramp).
- Net cash delta: +$130k/mo on current bookings; however pipeline seasonality could flip this in Q3.

Spend highlights / areas of concern:
1) Cloud infra (AWS+k8s spots + EFS): $420k/mo, +14% MoM due to increased training/inference spikes. Root cause: higher peak inference for enterprise customers (longer contexts). Ops investigating autoscale misconfigs.
2) Dedicated GPU reservations (partner/enterprise): $160k/mo committed; renewals in May for two customers (~$45k + $60k ARR each). Need to confirm renewal discounts and SLA credits.
3) Observability & analytics retention: $35k/mo current; proposal to extend 90-day retention for key customers -> incremental $18k/mo (contract change + procurement approval).
4) Third-party license renewals: Datadog, Snyk, PagerDuty — consolidated renewal window in June (estimated $210k/yr).

Procurement items requiring approval (ask of CPO):
- Item A: Purchase reserved GPU capacity for private deployments (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) to support an upcoming partner POC.
  - Ask: one-time CAPEX request: $1.2M (or commit to 12-month reserved contract ~$100k/mo).
  - Rationale: enable predictable performance SLAs for partner POC and convert to Dedicated customers.
  - Risk: large short-term cash outflow; alternative is burst-on-demand (higher per-token cost) and potential missed SLA.

- Item B: Increase analytics retention for top 10 enterprise customers
  - Ask: SaaS add-on contract amendment + procurement to increase logging/warehouse retention -> incremental $18k/mo.
  - Rationale: support quality/regression tooling and customer observability requirements.
  - Risk: modest ongoing cost; needs product confirmation that this is deliverable within current infra.

Questions I want to surface / confirm during 1:1:
- CPO tolerance for front-loading CAPEX vs prefer monthly committed spend? (Does leadership prefer preserving cash?)
- Priority: GPU capacity for POC vs faster time-to-value for multiple smaller customers (tradeoff: one big partner vs several small).
- Any planned hiring/pause that affects run-rate assumptions (SWE hiring + applied ML).
- Are we comfortable with proposed retention increase as a strategic differentiator for enterprise deals?

Quick notes to self (talking points):
- Emphasize conversion uplift: POC -> Dedicated conversion historically ~30% within 6 months. If true, justify CAPEX as investment.
- Show sensitivity: if we delay reserved purchase, estimated additional variable spend = +$40k/mo for next 6 months and potential SLA breaches for partner.
- Highlight renewals window in May/June and need close cross-functional support (account execs + solutions engineering).

Action items to close after meeting:
- Jordan: get CPO directional approval on procurement path (capex vs committed spend) -> target by Fri EOD.
- Aisha: pull detailed cost vs variable spend model for reserved GPU decision (spreadsheet link in Confluence) -> due Mon.
- Marco: confirm infra team's ETA on autoscale fixes + short-term mitigation to avoid cloud spikes -> due Tue.
- Jordan: draft proposed procurement approval memo (one-pager for Execs) with recommended option and risks -> due Wed.

Loose TODOs / follow-ups (personal scratchpad style):
- Check with Legal on contract amendment language for analytics retention (T&C impacts).
- Ask Sales Ops for list of top 10 enterprise customers impacted and current contract end dates.
- Add a sensitivity table (best/worst/likely) to the memo showing P&L impact over 12 months.

Notes from previous meeting (Feb status):
- FP&A asked to include scenario where two mid-market deals slip by quarter -> modeled as -$220k ARR.
- Engineering asked for 8-week lead time to provision reserved clusters. If procurement delayed, lead time pushes to Q4.

Tone: keep this light in the 1:1 — goal is directional buy-in, not final exec approval. Need to get alignment on approach so I can circulate a clean memo next week.

References/links: Confluence run-rate model, JIRA tickets for infra autoscale (JIRA-7831), procurement ticket (PROC-2026).

End of notes.
